newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent rallies after NYMEX finds support.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent rallies after NYMEX finds support.

text.p: IPE Brent futures rallied after the NYMEX opening on Tuesday, boosted by the failure of sellers to breach key support levels on the U.S. market, traders said.
Front-month May IPE Brent was trading 12 cents higher at $19.71 a barrel at 1530 GMT, around the day's highs.
Traders said the failure of early selling to get below $20.96 on front-month May NYMEX crude triggered buying that helped lift May IPE into positive territory for the first time in the session.
Further support came from news of plans for a big strike by up to 20 million people in Russian on Thursday to protest against wage arrears and government policy.
"I think some bulls began putting the Russian story about to talk it up," a trader said.
April IPE gas oil was trading $1.75 higher at $172.50 a tonne, around $1 above its morning levels.
Brent's revival was assisted by news that five of 12 Brent cargoes overhanging the wet market were sold to a U.S. refiner on a Dated Brent-related basis on Monday evening, trader said.
"It picked up a little bit with talk that BP had sold some of their cargoes," a trader said.

Overall fundamentals remain weak, with a glut of physical North Sea barrels weighing heavily on the market, and ample supplies of West African grades despite disruptions to Shell's Nigerian production due to a dispute between local villagers.
Shell Nigeria said that it expected to meet all its March export commitments.

Volume was thin, with players awaiting U.S. stock data due out later on Tuesday. Dealers expected trade to be rangebound ahead of the release after the close on Tuesday of weekly U.S. stocks data from the American Petroleum Institute (API).
